chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibrahim ibn Abi Sammal from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Then descend walking, and upon you be composure and dignity, until you reach the minaret, which is the end of the running ground (Mas'a), so run with the fullness of your stride and say: 'In the name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, and may Allah bless Muhammad and his family,' and say: 'O Allah, forgive, have mercy, and pardon what You know, for You are the Most Mighty, the Most Generous,' until you reach the other minaret.
He said: 'And the running ground was wider than it is today, but the people narrowed it.'
Then walk, and upon you be composure and dignity, until you reach Al-Marwah, so ascend it until the House becomes visible to you, and do upon it as you did upon As-Safa.
Then circumambulate between them seven circuits, starting with As-Safa and concluding with Al-Marwah.
Then trim from your head from its sides, and from your beard, and take from your mustache, and clip your nails, and leave them for your Hajj.
So when you do that, you have released yourself from everything from which the Muhrim releases, and you have entered the state of Ihram for it.

key_terms.أَحْلَلْتَ: You have released/disembarked (from the state of Ihram restrictions)
key_terms.الْمَنَارَة: The minaret or marker indicating the end of the running ground
key_terms.الْمُحْرِم: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What are the specific supplications and physical actions required during the Sa'i ritual in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific etiquette of Sa'i, emphasizing the transition from solemn composure (sakinah) to vigorous running (mil'a furujik) between the Safa and Marwah markers. It highlights the historical context that the original distance was wider before people narrowed it, and concludes with the ritual acts of cutting hair and nails that signify the pilgrim's release from the state of Ihram.
